course_summary:
ISEN 640 | Systems Thinking and Analysis | Fall 2026
Instructor: Joseph Geunes | geunes@tamu.edu, Richard Mayer | ricmayer@tamu.edu
Meets: N/A | ONLINE
Grading: Exam 1 [25%], Exam 2 [25%], Homework [50%] — A: 90% - 100%, B: 80% - 89.9%, C: 70% - 79.9%, D: 60% - 69.9%, F: below 60%
Topics: Complex Adaptive Systems Definition, Complex Adaptive Systems Development, Model Based Systems Engineering, Model Based Decision Making, Systems Description Languages, Theory of Systems Design, System Architectures, Engineered Systems Life Cycle, Engineered Systems Development, Documenting the SE Process, anatomy of engineered systems, complex interactions, formulate issues, analyze issues, interpret issues, separate symptoms, concerns, opportunities, diagnose causes, identify causes, problem, systems thinking techniques, systems thinking methods, critical thinking techniques, model engineered systems, critique engineered systems, analyze engineered systems, multidisciplinary teams, communicate ideas verbally, communicate ideas in writing, national systems engineering issues, global systems engineering issues, Introduction to Systems Thinking & Analysis, Methods for Systems Thinking and Analysis, Systems Modeling, Systems Thinking in Engineering Design, Trade-offs, systems thinking process, engineering of large-scale systems, systems engineering practice, systems engineering methods, systems engineering tools, systems engineering
Tools: Canvas
Prerequisites: MATH 304 or approval of instructor
